name: The adjective like the participle (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha)
definition: An adjective made from an intransitive verb that names a lasting quality, such as ḥasan, 'handsome', from ḥasuna: 'likened' to the active participle because it governs as it does.
body: Where the active participle (ḍārib) names someone doing something at a time, the ṣifa mushabbaha names a quality that lasts. It is mostly made from verbs of the bāb of karuma and samiʿa, on patterns that are learnt by hearing: ḥasan, karīm, ṣaʿb and many more. In naḥw it governs a noun after it in three ways (ḥasanu al-wajhi, ḥasanun wajhuhu, ḥasanun wajhan), which the Alfiyya treats in its own chapter.

examples.text: ḥasuna, 'to be handsome', and the adjective ḥasan.
